The climate in Smolyan

Smolyan is about 950 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 25°C; the coldest is January, when nights average −3°C. Around 990 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in June (about 122 mm). The highest temperature in Smolyan in 2015–2024 was 34°C (2 August 2021) and the lowest −19°C (8 January 2017).

Smolyan stretches along a long valley in the Central Rhodopes at about 1000 m and is the highest regional city in Bulgaria. Summers are cool and fresh, and winters are snowy. Moist air from the Mediterranean reaches the Rhodopes, so the town gets much more precipitation than the lowlands to the north.

Best time to visit Smolyan

The most pleasant weather in Smolyan is usually in July, August and September: average highs are between 21°C and 25°C, with up to 9 days of rain a month. In January nights are frosty (below −3°C on average) and snow is common.
